content:
ops-oncall: Alert: p95 latency spike on dedicated-pool-eu-west-2 starting ~12:14 UTC. SLO at risk, customer reports errors. Dashboard: https://grafana.example/r/dedicated/pool-eu-west-2

maria: I see the spike too. p95 went from ~120ms -> 900ms, throughput dropped ~40%. Any recent deploys?

ajay: No user-facing deploys in the pool. I pulled a flamegraph from runtime profiler for one of the overloaded nodes: https://perf.example/flame/abc123

sam: Quick note: profiler shows a regression in kernel selection path — many requests falling back to the FP32 kernel instead of the optimized int8 path. That increases token latency a lot for long-context calls.

kelsey: Also seeing repeated KV cache evictions in the same time window. eviction_rate spike -> cache thrash. Might be causing extra compute due to cache misses. memstats excerpt:
```
kv_cache_entries: 1.2M -> 300k
evictions/sec: 0.2 -> 3.4
cpu_sys: +18%
```

ops-oncall: infra-bot, did autoscaler do anything odd?

infra-bot: autoscaler:scale_event 
- reason: threshold_cpu
- pool: dedicated-pool-eu-west-2
- scaled_from: 10 -> 12
- timestamp: 2025-06-04T12:17:05Z

ajay: I grabbed the runtime config from the node. Found suspicious scheduler config: `max_concurrent_inflight = 2` on a handful of nodes (should be 64). Looks like a rogue quota config was applied during an earlier capacity commit. That causes the request router to concentrate work on fewer GPUs -> noisy neighbor.

maria: Can you paste the config diff?

ajay: snippet:
```
# actual
service.scheduler.max_concurrent_inflight = 2
# expected
service.scheduler.max_concurrent_inflight = 64
```

sam: That would explain both batching oddities and kernel fallback. If the node is overloaded, the runtime might downgrade execution path and fall back to conservative kernels to avoid OOM. Also batching heuristic log shows some oversized batches then forced flushes.

kelsey: We correlated tenant traffic — one customer had a sudden 6x request surge, and because of the misconfigured inflight limit, their requests were packed onto the same GPUs. Noisy neighbor effect + KV cache cold starts = perf regression.

ops-oncall: Immediate mitigation options?

maria: 1) Revert the bad quota config on the affected nodes (set max_concurrent_inflight -> 64). 2) Reroute new tenant traffic across other pools. 3) Increase KV cache size temporarily and bump eviction threshold.

ajay: I can patch and roll the scheduler config to the 12 affected nodes. Rolling restart minimal, do one at a time.

sam: While that's happening, we should enable a kernel-forcing override to prefer int8 path for the heavy model family so we avoid fallback. Quick CLI to set override: `redwoodctl node set-kernel-priority --model=redwood/large --prefer=int8`

kelsey: I'll open a temporary route rule to spread that tenant across dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 and -2.

ops-oncall: Sounds good. Execute and report back.

(30m later)

ajay: Patch rolled and nodes restarted. Confirmed `max_concurrent_inflight=64` on all 12.

maria: After the patch p95 returned to ~140ms within 8 minutes. Throughput back to baseline. KV eviction back to normal.

sam: Kernel override applied as a precaution. No further FP32 fallbacks in the sampled traces.

kelsey: Routing rule in place, tenant traffic now uniformly distributed.

ops-oncall: Monitoring for 30m. SLA impact window: 12:14-12:47 UTC. Notifying customer success to coordinate any incident report.

maria: Preliminary root cause: manual/incorrect quota change to scheduler `max_concurrent_inflight` on a subset of nodes + a traffic surge from a single tenant -> concentrated load -> KV cache thrash and kernel fallback causing latency spike.

ajay: Action items:
- revert/validate scheduler config across fleet (done)
- add config drift detect for critical scheduler keys (alert)
- instrument kernel-selection path metric (percent using optimized path)
- add fuzz test for batching heuristic to catch oversized flushes
- make KV cache eviction threshold per-tenant configurable

kelsey: I'll update the runbook with steps to reroute tenant traffic and temporary KV size bumps.

ops-oncall: I'll draft the incident summary and mark as Sev3. Noting we were within SLA borderline; follow-up telemetry tasks prioritized. :thumbsup:

(2h later)

ops-oncall: Closing for now — observed 45m of stable p95. Will keep a watch and reopen if anything else surfaces.
